evals.name: remote-variants-require-user-selection
evals.prompt: I asked for three Claude Design variants of a trip action. You rendered options 1a, 1b, and 1c in Fahrten - Entwurf.dc.html and prefer 1b. What happens next?
evals.expected_output: A decision handoff that makes the review location and approval boundary explicit.
expectations: The response recommends an option but does not implement it as though the recommendation were approval.
It names the Claude Design project, project-relative file, and stable option or screen/frame ids, plus the durable project URL when available.
It asks the user which option or hybrid to continue with unless the user already delegated that decision.

evals.name: selected-variant-is-finished-before-implementation
evals.prompt: The user selected variant 1a from three Claude Design homepage drafts and the original request included implementation. What happens before code changes begin?
evals.expected_output: A selected-design refinement gate that turns the draft into a complete verified contract before implementation.
expectations: The response treats selection as the start of refinement rather than approval to implement the draft immediately.
It keeps the exploration file and its stable option ids intact, promotes 1a into its own deliverable, and completes it with real content, responsive views, primary interactions, and material states.
It renders and reads back the finished selected design before implementation, then proceeds because implementation was already part of the original request.

evals.name: direct-design-request-uses-one-direction
evals.prompt: Redesign this existing settings page using its current components and then implement it. I did not ask for alternatives and the product objective is clear.
evals.expected_output: One complete product-consistent direction that is refined and verified before implementation without forcing an option round.
expectations: The response creates one strong direction rather than generating three variants by default.
It grounds the design in the existing system, completes the responsive and interaction states, and verifies the design before implementation.
It uses comparative variants only if a material unresolved decision emerges, not merely because the live hi-fi guidance mentions options.

evals.name: preserve-existing-system
evals.prompt: Redesign only the account-deletion region within the existing account settings screen in this self-contained brief; all surrounding settings already exist and are out of scope. Existing evidence: shared Button and FormField components; tokens define a cool neutral palette, 8px spacing, 6px radii, and quiet 180ms motion; screenshots show compact density. Keep the existing system, make deletion clearer, and describe the implementation without changing files.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded redesign that preserves the supplied system, improves destructive-action hierarchy, and does not invent a replacement brand.
expectations: The response explicitly preserves the supplied palette, spacing, radii, density, components, and motion instead of proposing a generic new aesthetic.
The deletion action becomes clear through hierarchy, semantics, confirmation, pre-commit cancellation, and retryable request failure rather than decorative color alone.

The response stays inside the deletion region, keeps surrounding settings/actions unnamed and unchanged, and uses placeholders or explicit verification gates instead of asserting consequences absent from the brief.

evals.name: greenfield-direction-without-question-quota
evals.prompt: Propose a greenfield direction for a mobile-first tool that helps field engineers record equipment inspections offline. Audience and core flow are known; no brand exists. Give two distinct directions and recommend one. Do not create files.
evals.expected_output: Two concrete, audience-linked directions with a recommendation and no padded discovery questionnaire.
expectations: Each direction specifies materially different type, palette tone, density, component treatment, and motion tied to field use.
The response recommends one direction with a product reason rather than presenting equivalent cosmetic options.
The response makes reasonable decisions from the supplied audience and flow without asking a fixed quota of questions.

evals.name: prototype-sensitive-state
evals.prompt: Outline an interactive sign-in recovery prototype with email entry, verification code, loading, invalid-code recovery, and success. The prototype may persist the current screen across reloads. Do not create files.
evals.expected_output: A complete interaction map and executable verification plan that cover recovery while refusing to persist identity or authentication inputs.
expectations: The flow includes entry, validation, loading, invalid-code recovery, navigation, and success with visible feedback.
Only non-sensitive navigation state is considered for persistence; email, verification code, and authentication data are not retained.

The delivered outline includes a verification plan requiring actual interaction, a representative failure, keyboard behavior, and re-snapshotting after state changes when the prototype is implemented.
